# PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS

## Scope of this Part and interpretation

## 70.1

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.1] (1) This Part contains general rules about enforcement of judgments and orders.

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.1] (Rules about specific methods of enforcement are contained in Parts 71 to 73, 81, 83, 84 and 89, and Schedule 2 CCR Order 28)

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.1] (2) In this Part and in Parts 71 to 73 –

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.1] (a) ‘judgment creditor’ means a person who has obtained or is entitled to enforce a judgment or order;

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.1] (b) ‘judgment debtor’ means a person against whom a judgment or order was given or made;

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.1] (c) ‘judgment or order’ includes an award which the court has –

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.1] (i) registered for enforcement;

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.1] (ii) ordered to be enforced; or

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.1] (iii) given permission to enforce

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.1] as if it were a judgment or order of the court, and in relation to such an award, ‘the court which made the judgment or order’ means the court which registered the award or made such an order; and

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.1] (ca) “judgment or order” also includes an award enforceable under the Judgments Regulation (Regulation (EU) No. 1215/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 12 December 2012 on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters (recast)(1)) as if it were an order or judgment of the court, and in relation to such an award “the court which made the judgment or order” means the county court or the High Court.

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.1] (d) ‘judgment or order for the payment of money’ includes a judgment or order for the payment of costs, but does not include a judgment or order for the payment of money into court.

## Application for order

## 70.1A

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.1A] (1) In this rule, reference to a fine is to a fine imposed under the County Courts Act 1984.

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.1A] (2) If a fine is not paid in accordance with the order imposing it, the court officer shall, as soon as reasonably possible, report the matter to a judge.

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.1A] (3) Where a fine is directed to be paid by instalments, default in the payment of any instalment may be taken as if default had been made in payment of the whole of the fine.

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.1A] (4) If an order is made for payment of a fine to be enforced by warrant of control, the order shall be treated as an application to the court for the issue of the warrant at the time when the order was made.

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.1A] (5) If a person pays a fine and later gives evidence to satisfy the court that, if the evidence had been given earlier, no fine or a smaller fine would have been imposed, the court may order the whole or part of the fine to be repaid.

## Methods of enforcing judgments or orders

## 70.2

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.2] (1) Practice Direction 70 sets out methods of enforcing judgments or orders for the payment of money.

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.2] (2) A judgment creditor may, except where an enactment, rule or practice direction provides otherwise –

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.2] (a) use any method of enforcement which is available; and

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.2] (b) use more than one method of enforcement, either at the same time or one after another.

## Court may order act to be done at expense of disobedient party

## 70.2A

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.2A] (1) In this rule ‘disobedient party’ means a party who has not complied with a mandatory order, an injunction or a judgment or order for the specific performance of a contract.

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.2A] (2) Subject to paragraph (4), if a mandatory order, an injunction or a judgment or order for the specific performance of a contract is not complied with, the court may direct that the act required to be done may, so far as practicable, be done by another person, being—

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.2A] (a) the party by whom the order or judgment was obtained; or

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.2A] (b) some other person appointed by the court.

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.2A] (3) Where paragraph (2) applies—

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.2A] (a) the costs to another person of doing the act will be borne by the disobedient party

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.2A] (b) upon the act being done the expenses incurred may be ascertained in such manner as the court directs; and

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.2A] (c) execution may issue against the disobedient party for the amount so ascertained and for costs.

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.2A] (4) Paragraph (2) is without prejudice to—

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.2A] (a) the court’s powers under section 39 of the Senior Courts Act 1981 1 ; and

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.2A] (b) the court’s powers to punish the disobedient party for contempt.

## Transfer of proceedings for enforcement

## 70.3

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.3] (1) Subject to rule 83.17, a judgment creditor wishing to enforce a High Court judgment or order in the County Court must apply to the High Court for an order transferring the proceedings.

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.3] (2) A practice direction may make provisions about the transfer of proceedings for enforcement.

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.3] (Rule 83.19 contains provisions about the transfer of County Court proceedings to the High Court for enforcement.)

## Enforcement of judgment or order by or against non-party

## 70.4

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.4] If a judgment or order is given or made in favour of or against a person who is not a party to proceedings, it may be enforced by or against that person by the same methods as if he were a party.

## 70.5

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.5] (1) This rule applies, subject to paragraph (2), where an enactment provides that –

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.5] (a) a decision of a court, tribunal, body or person other than the High Court or the County Court; or

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.5] (b) a compromise,

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.5] may be enforced as if it were a court order or that any sum of money payable under that decision or compromise may be recoverable as if payable under a court order.

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.5] (2) This rule does not apply to –

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.5] (a) any judgment to which Part 74 applies;

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.5] (b) arbitration awards;

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.5] (c) any order to which RSC Order 115 applies; or

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.5] (d) proceedings to which Part 75 (traffic enforcement) applies.

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.5] (2A) Unless paragraph (3) applies, a party may enforce the decision or compromise by applying for a specific method of enforcement under Parts 71 to 73, 81, 83, 84 and 89, and Schedule 2 CCR Order 28 and must –

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.5] (a) file with the court a copy of the decision or compromise being enforced; and

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.5] (b) provide the court with the information required by Practice Direction 70.

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.5] (3) If an enactment provides that a decision or compromise is enforceable or a sum of money is recoverable if a court so orders, an application for such an order must be made in accordance with paragraphs (4) to (7A) of this rule.

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.5] (4) The application –

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.5] (a) may, unless paragraph (4A) applies, be made without notice; and

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.5] (b) must be made to the court for the district where the person against whom the order is sought, resides or carries on business, unless an enactment, rule or practice direction provides otherwise or the court otherwise orders.

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.5] (4A) Where a compromise requires a person to whom a sum of money is payable under the compromise to do anything in addition to discontinuing or not starting proceedings (‘a conditional compromise’), an application under paragraph (4) must be made on notice.

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.5] (5) The application notice must –

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.5] (a) be in the form; and

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.5] (b) contain the information

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.5] required by Practice Direction 70.

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.5] (6) A copy of the decision or compromise must be filed with the application notice.

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.5] (7) An application other than in relation to a conditional compromise may be dealt with by a court officer without a hearing.

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.5] (7A) Where an application relates to a conditional compromise, the respondent may oppose it by filing a response within 14 days of service of the application notice and if the respondent –

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.5] (a) does not file a response within the time allowed, the court will make the order; or

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.5] (b) files a response within the time allowed, the court will make such order as appears appropriate.

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.5] (8) If an enactment provides that a decision or compromise may be enforced in the same manner as an order of the High Court if it is registered, any application to the High Court for registration must be made in accordance with Practice Direction 70.

## Effect of setting aside judgment or order

## 70.6

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.6] If a judgment or order is set aside, any enforcement of the judgment or order shall cease to have effect unless the court otherwise orders.

## Debt respite scheme

## 70.7

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.7] (1) A practice direction may make provision for procedure relating to any debt respite scheme established under section 7 of the Financial Guidance and Claims Act 2018(2).

[PART 70 – GENERAL RULES ABOUT ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS > 70.7] (2) The practice direction may modify or disapply any provision of these Rules as appropriate in relation to such a debt respite scheme.

## Footnotes
